system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A higher, commercially meaningful general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental, tax, specific indemnity and other agreed risk categories. | **Reject 20%; seek a materially higher cap.** AUD 4.8m may be inadequate against unknown business-wide warranty exposure. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping/excess-only basket. | A lower de minimis and a tipping basket, or no basket for significant or specified claims; clarify aggregation and related claims. | **Counter on both thresholds and make the basket tipping.** Excess-only recovery leaves the buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying losses. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller also proposes all Claims share any applicable limitation unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with separate, appropriate survival periods for tax, fundamental/title, and specific indemnity claims; preserve statutory periods where relevant. | **Reject the blanket rule and negotiate category-specific periods.** The proposal risks applying a short general deadline to claims that need longer periods to emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher cap (potentially up to price or agreed recovery), and longer survival for capacity, authority and title; specific treatment for tax and indemnities. | **Reject parity with general warranties.** Defects in ownership or authority strike at the transaction itself and warrant stronger protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Expressly exclude fraud (and, as negotiated, wilful misconduct) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, subject to applicable law. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** Otherwise the draft may purport to restrict remedies for deliberate deception. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-records disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and retain only sufficiently specific disclosures.** A document dump makes it unclear which warranty risks were actually disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No broad imputed or constructive knowledge bar; at most, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named individuals after specified disclosure, without limiting claims for fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the proposed qualifier.** “Discoverable” knowledge and adviser knowledge can defeat warranties without clear, actual awareness. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and no final consent or evidence conditions were met. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of clause 11.3 conditions before Completion; termination or other protection if unmet. | **Make compliant consent and conditions a Completion condition.** Bluefen represents about 30% of revenue, so a mere endeavours obligation is insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released following Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding with no final discharge or security release. | Repayment from Completion funds (or before Completion), lender payout and irrevocable discharge/release of all security as a Completion deliverable; no post-Completion reliance on Seller. | **Require payoff and release at Completion, with funds-flow mechanics.** A promise of later release leaves the acquired company exposed to debt and encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses omitted from draft funds flow; tax and on-cost treatment unspecified. Seller says they are its matter and not separately itemised. | Identify the obligation, determine payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, and ensure the price/funds flow accounts for all amounts; Seller funds or indemnifies any agreed seller-borne liability. | **Do not accept the omission: quantify and allocate the full cost before signing/Completion.** The stated AUD 420,000 may understate the target’s actual liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004/010 show AUD 180,000 open, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering all losses from failure to obtain the SOW3 Project Materials, including unpaid fees, remediation, replacement, third-party claims and enforcement costs; secure assignment on cleared payment. | **Expand and preserve the indemnity, and make transfer evidence a Completion deliverable.** The open fee and absent assignment leave ownership and usable-IP risk unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises DD-006 as preliminary and not expected material; facts do not establish access, scope or notification requirement. | Full investigation and incident records; appropriate remediation/notifications; targeted warranty and specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident and resulting claims, costs and regulatory exposure, with no materiality assumption. | **Seek a specific incident protection and verified status before Completion.** Uncertainty about access and 1,240 potentially affected records is not evidence of immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330,000, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. | Confirm terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and whether commitments are assumed in the price; include unpaid or non-ordinary-course amounts in debt-like items or specific protection as appropriate. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without verification.** The records do not establish the buyer’s actual post-Completion commitment or price treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to Claims “of any nature”; Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Define separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with expressly tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies. | **Reject all-Claims treatment and document each category separately.** A single general regime can unintentionally dilute negotiated protections for distinct risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify the register, constitution, issue history, encumbrances and transfer authority; obtain title/authority warranties and duly executed transfer instruments at Completion. | **Treat DD-012 as evidence, not complete verification.** The disclosure itself does not establish independent verification or eliminate competing title/encumbrance risk. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime, but no detailed terms are provided here. | Keep these as open drafting/negotiation items: review tax warranties and any tax indemnity, IP ownership/chain-of-title warranties and specific protections, with tailored caps and survival periods. | **Do not mark settled on this record; reserve and negotiate expressly.** The update supplies no substantive tax/IP terms sufficient to assess or accept. |

These are buyer-side negotiating positions based on the supplied update and disclosure letter, not a review of the complete SPA or underlying due diligence documents.
=== END ADVICE ===
